decisions.headline: Since 14 Oct, iOS checkout in London and Barcelona has been converting at about 22% instead of 62%, which costs about €1.5M of revenue a month. That has to be fixed before any budget move, and it is a fix for engineering, not for marketing.

data_sufficiency.explanation: The checkout break and the Berlin stock-out are solid. I checked both in sales_daily and products: London iOS had 26,402 checkouts and 5,825 orders, Barcelona iOS 14,143 checkouts and 3,082 orders, Paris iOS stayed normal at 62.1%, and BER-HOM-E10 had 219 units of stock against 6,761 normally. The mix model is only directional. Search interest drives most of its fit (elasticity about 0.96), S fffffffffffffe3o Paulo and Miami are probably overfit, and Beauty plus London and New York Fashion drops fit poorly. The unit_costs table is empty, so every figure is revenue, not gross profit. ux_daily and events_daily are empty, so I cannot say which checkout step fails.

findings.title: iOS checkout broken in London and Barcelona since 2026-10-14
findings.evidence: London iOS went from 62.0% to 22.1% (n=26,402 checkouts) and Barcelona iOS from 62.2% to 21.8% (n=14,143). Android, desktop and Paris iOS are unchanged. Lost orders are about 10.5k in London and 5.7k in Barcelona over 19 days, at an average order of about €60, which is about €1.0M plus €0.54M a month. Customer comments about payment problems rose from 6 to 19 in London and from 3 to 15 in Barcelona ('payment page froze', 'card declined').

findings.title: Berlin Home has had nothing to sell since 23 Oct because of a stock-setting error
findings.evidence: BER-HOM-E10 had 219 units of stock against 6,761 for E08, E09 and E11, and sold out 4 days after launch. Revenue per day went from €13.6k to €7.3k, while Amsterdam Home (control) rose. Lost revenue is about €188k a month. 'Sold out' comments made up 23.6% of Berlin Home comments (13 of 55). Berlin Home spend was about €56k over the last 28 days and is still running.

findings.title: Moving money between channels at the same total budget looks worth about €360k a month in the well-fitting lines (model estimate, before any haircut)
findings.evidence: That is €83k a week across 12 lines with a fit (r2) of at least 0.7, and €143k a week across the 19 visible lines. Last-click credits Google brand with a 8.95 return per euro, but the model says the next euro adds 0–1.4. Meta retargeting: Meta reports 3.41, our own data 1.55, the model 0.1–1.65. YouTube, creators and TikTok return 2.8–9.07 per extra euro. The plan's increases (55–70%) go beyond spend the model has seen, so the planner expects the real gain could be about half.

findings.title: Madrid Fashion drops captures only 72% of its search demand, and extra spend there still pays
findings.evidence: 16.0 orders per 1,000 searches against 22.2 for peers; the gap is €560.8k over 8 weeks. Checkout is normal (61.9%). The next euro returns 2.74 (YouTube 7.32). Spend was €57.4k over 28 days.

findings.title: Beauty earns the least per extra euro
findings.evidence: Return on the next euro: Lisbon Beauty 0.97, Amsterdam 1.07, Berlin 1.18, Barcelona 1.01 (pulled down by the checkout break). Spend over 28 days: Lisbon €45.3k, Amsterdam €55.9k.

findings.title: New York organic search fell, and customers report broken Google links
findings.evidence: Organic search revenue was €581.7k against €757.3k in the prior 28 days and €923.1k last year; sessions fell from 607k to 462k. 37 of 233 comments (15.9%) mention a broken link from Google, against 3.7% in other markets.

findings.title: Lisbon: late deliveries and a drop in email orders
findings.evidence: Late-delivery comments: 64 of 213 (30%) against 6.2% before. NPS went from -32 to -39. Email orders fell from 1,415 to 945 (-33%), about €29k a month. Revenue per day is €34.7k against €37.4k last year.

findings.title: Rain clearly lifts Home and Gifts sales in all 11 markets with weather data; it lowers Fashion drops
findings.evidence: Gifts: London +33.1%, Berlin +30.5% [26.8, 34.3], Amsterdam +27.8% [24.2, 31.5]. São Paulo Home +18.3%, with 8 rainy days in the 14-day forecast. Fashion drops falls 4.5–9.6% with rain, and Beauty's effect is too small to act on.

findings.title: Seasonal or ramp-up, not problems: Berlin's overall decline and Mexico City
findings.evidence: Berlin's 25% fall matches last year's 21% fall over the same weeks. Mexico City is at 5% of earlier launches at the same age, but its CPA improved from €55 to €38. It has no mix model yet, so I am not changing its budget.

recommendations.action: Raise a P1 incident with engineering to fix iOS checkout and payment in London and Barcelona.
recommendations.why: iOS checkout-to-order fell from 62% to about 22% on 2026-10-14 in only these two markets. Android, desktop and Paris are unaffected, and customers report the payment page freezing and cards being declined.
recommendations.expected_impact: About €1.5M of revenue a month recovered (about €1.0M London, €0.54M Barcelona). The CPA and MER for both markets also return to normal.
recommendations.how_to_measure: Daily iOS checkout-to-order in London and Barcelona, back to about 62%.
recommendations.metric_sql: SELECT 1.0*SUM(orders)/SUM(checkouts) AS value FROM sales_daily WHERE device='ios' AND market IN ('London','Barcelona') AND day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM sales_daily),'-7 days')

execution.note: P1, markets London and Barcelona. Since 2026-10-14, iOS checkout-to-order is 22.1% in London (26,402 checkouts → 5,825 orders) and 21.8% in Barcelona (14,143 → 3,082), against about 62% before and on Android, desktop and Paris iOS. Customers report the payment page freezing and cards declined on mobile. Check releases, payment-provider changes, Apple Pay and Safari changes around 14 Oct, then roll back or hotfix. About €1.5M of revenue a month is lost.

recommendations.action: Apply the mix model's channel reallocation across the portfolio, each line's total unchanged, with no channel moved by more than 25%.
recommendations.why: Google brand (model's next-euro return 0–1.4) and Meta retargeting (0.1–1.65) are overfunded. YouTube, creators and TikTok (2.8–9.07) are underfunded. Twelve lines fit well (r2 ≥ 0.7). The 25% cap keeps spend close to levels the model has seen.
recommendations.expected_impact: The model estimates about €360k a month in the well-fitting lines at its full moves. With the 25% cap and the planner's warning that the real gain could be half, I expect less than that. Spend stays the same.
recommendations.how_to_measure: Portfolio revenue per € of ad spend over 28 days, against the current baseline. Read it alongside the checkout fix, which also lifts revenue.
recommendations.metric_sql: SELECT (SELECT SUM(revenue) FROM sales_daily WHERE day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM sales_daily),'-28 days')) / (SELECT SUM(spend) FROM ad_daily WHERE day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM ad_daily),'-28 days')) AS value

execution.note: Portfolio-wide, so leadership approves. Leave out poorly fitting lines (London and New York Fashion drops, London Home, Beauty except Berlin) and Mexico City, which has no model. Judge results on first-party revenue, not on what platforms report.

input.brief: Data runs to 2026-11-01. Compare the 12 markets x 4 product lines over the last 4 weeks vs the prior 4 weeks: revenue, gross profit, spend, ROAS/CPA, conversion. Identify market-lines that capture much less of their potential demand than peers (use market_profile / search_interest), and any ads far above target CPA, fatigued, or broken. Quantify € at stake per month for each issue, with n. Flag anything that is a non-marketing problem (stock-outs, site/checkout issues) with market and evidence.

Data runs to 2026-11-01. Assess demand drivers per market-line: measured weather (rain) effect on sales with sign and confidence, holidays/seasonality to separate from real trends, search interest trends. Tell me which market-lines have a clearly positive rain effect (candidates for a weather rule) and which do not. Also flag stock events / limited-edition sell-outs that cap demand, with € impact per month.

Data runs to 2026-11-01. Analyze voc_items / voc_labels for the last 4-8 weeks: top complaint themes by market and product, trends vs prior period, anything pointing to product defects, delivery/logistics, checkout or site bugs, or ad/landing mismatch. Give counts (n), affected markets/products, and the likely revenue impact. Recommend which team should own each fix.

Data runs to 2026-11-01. ~€3.3M/month spend. Report your marketing-mix model fit by market-line (which fits are good vs poor), the channel reallocation it recommends with marginal ROAS per channel, and expected revenue/GP gain at constant budget. Identify market-lines with high marginal returns that are underfunded vs potential, and lines with low marginal returns that could fund them. Also check budget pacing (v_budget_pacing) for over/under-pacing. Give € numbers.

findings.title: iOS checkout broken in London and Barcelona since 2026-10-14
findings.evidence: London iOS went from 62.0% to 22.1% (n=26,402 checkouts) and Barcelona iOS from 62.2% to 21.8% (n=14,143). Android, desktop and Paris iOS are unchanged. findings.title: Berlin Home has had nothing to sell since 23 Oct because of a stock-setting error

findings.title: Moving money between channels at the same total budget looks worth about €360k a month in the well-fitting lines (model estimate, before any haircut)

findings.title: Beauty earns the least per extra euro

input.summary: The biggest issue is a broken iOS checkout in London and Barcelona: since 2026-10-14, iOS checkout-to-order is about 22%, against 62% on Android, desktop, peers and last year. This costs roughly €1.5M of revenue a month and is a site problem, not a marketing one. The other outliers are smaller: a drop in Lisbon email and repeat orders, and a Mexico City launch running at 5% of earlier launches. Berlin's fall is the same seasonal dip it had last year.

findings.line: all lines (all 4 lines show checkout-to-order down from 61.8–62.5% to 48.3–49.7%)
findings.evidence: iOS checkout-to-order was 34.6% over the last 4 weeks against 62.0% in the prior 4 weeks, 62.2% last year and a peer range of 61.98–62.10. From 10-14 on it was 22.1% (n=26,402 iOS checkouts, 5,825 orders). Android (61.9%) and desktop (61.7%) are normal. London revenue per day is €86.3k against €107.5k in the prior period and €107.1k last year. CPA rose to €22.29 from €17.24 (peer range 17.50–17.71) and MER fell to 7.09 from 9.12. All of this follows from orders lost at checkout, not from the ads. Sizing: 26,402 × (62.0% − 22.1%) ≈ 10.5k lost orders × AOV €60.1 ≈ €633k over 19 days, so about €1.0M a month.

It is improving: average revenue per day over the last 4 weeks was €10.2k against €3.4k before, and spend went from about €20k to €54k. The money at stake can't be sized reliably while the market is ramping.

input.summary: The biggest demand gaps are Madrid Fashion drops and Berlin Home. Madrid Fashion drops captures only 72% of its search demand (gap €560,836 over 8 weeks), and its last euro of spend still returns 2.74. Berlin Home revenue fell to about half after an edition with 219 units of stock (normally 6,761) sold out on 23 Oct. Rain clearly lifts Home and Gifts in all 11 markets with weather data, so these 22 market-lines are candidates for a weather rule. Rain clearly lowers Fashion drops sales, and Beauty's rain effect is too small to act on. The demand model is accurate enough to trust: 7.3% average error on held-out weeks.

findings.title: Edition with 219 units of stock sold out; Berlin Home revenue roughly halved
findings.evidence: BER-HOM-E10 had 219 units of stock, against 6,761 for every earlier and the next Berlin Home edition. It sold out on 2026-10-23, 4 days after launch, and the edition runs until 2026-11-29. Berlin Home revenue: 13,552 €/day the week before launch, 7,296 €/day from 24 Oct to 1 Nov. That is 14,586 €/day in the same period last year and 14,887 €/day for the peer median (peer range 13,529–16,245). Amsterdam Home, used as a control, went up over the same days (12,786 → 13,529 €/day). Search interest was flat against last year. Monthly impact: (13,552 − 7,296) × 30 ≈ €188k. The 8-week demand table still shows Berlin Home at 100% captured because only the last 9 days are affected.

findings.title: Madrid Fashion drops: steady shortfall in demand capture, not a fall in demand
findings.evidence: Captures 16.0 orders per 1,000 category searches against 22.2 for peers, i.e. 72% of potential. Gap: 9,677 orders / €560,836 over 8 weeks, the largest of any market-line. Revenue is 23,346 €/day, against 23,459 €/day last year. Checkout-to-order is 61.9%, against a peer median of 61.75%. So this is neither a recent drop nor a checkout fault; it is reach. The last euro of spend still returns 2.74 (4th best of 48), and the best channel, YouTube, returns 7.32. Monthly figure = 8-week gap × 30/56.

input.summary: Two checkout problems on iOS, both starting 2026-10-14, are the biggest issue. iOS checkout-to-order fell from about 62% to 35% in London and Barcelona, which works out to roughly €975k of lost revenue per 28 days, and customers there say the payment page froze or cards were declined. Next come Lisbon's delivery delays (64 mentions, about 3x the prior 28 days, NPS -39), broken Google links in New York (organic-search revenue down €176k vs the prior period) and Berlin Home selling out.

findings.title: iOS checkout/payment failure in London (owner: Engineering/Payments)
findings.evidence: payment_problem comments: 19 of 236 (8.1%) vs 2.4% in other markets, up from 6 in the prior 28 days. In Fashion drops: 9 of 61 (14.8%). What customers say: 'Payment page froze at checkout and the customer gave up', 'card declined three times, though it works elsewhere', 'payment repeatedly failed on their phone'. iOS checkout-to-order: 34.6% vs 62.1% in the prior period, 62.2% last year and 62.0% peer median. Android (61.8%) is normal. The first day below 50% was 2026-10-14. NPS fell from -15 to -35. iOS had 38,714 checkouts and 13,393 orders in the last 28 days; at the old 62% rate that is about 10.6k lost orders × €59.7 average order ≈ €634k per 28 days.

findings.title: The same iOS checkout failure in Barcelona, which the comment scan underplays (owner: Engineering/Payments)
findings.evidence: payment_problem comments: 15 in the last 28 days vs 3 before. Gist: 'payment page kept freezing', 'card showed an error', 'failed several times on mobile'. iOS checkout-to-order: 34.5% (7,166 orders from 20,768 checkouts) vs 62.2% before. Android and desktop are normal. Same start date, 2026-10-14, as London, so the cause is probably shared (an iOS release or payment-provider change). About 5.7k lost orders × €59.3 ≈ €341k per 28 days.

findings.title: Lisbon late deliveries, across every line (owner: Ops/Logistics)
findings.evidence: delivery_late: 64 of 213 comments (30.0%) vs 4.7% elsewhere and 6.2% before (22 in the prior 28 days). Weekly mentions rose from 1–8 to 13–20 from the week of 2026-10-05. Gist: 'still waiting for my order', 'arrived a week late'. NPS fell from -32 to -39. Revenue is €34.7k/day vs €36.9k in the prior period and €37.4k last year. The gap to last year is about €2.6k/day, roughly €73k per 28 days (partly attributable to delivery).

findings.title: Broken links from Google into the New York site (owner: Web/SEO)
findings.evidence: website_ux: 37 of 233 comments (15.9%) vs 3.7% elsewhere and 7.2% before. The gist is the same in almost every comment: 'couldn't find the page via Google because the link was broken'. Organic-search revenue is €582k in the last 28 days vs €757k in the prior 28 and €891k a year ago. Organic share is 42.7% vs 47.9% last year. Losing €176k vs the prior period points to dead URLs or redirects.

findings.title: Berlin Home hero product sold out early (owner: Merchandising/Supply)
findings.evidence: sold_out: 13 of 55 Home comments (23.6%) vs 4.0% elsewhere and 3.1% before. Across Berlin, sold_out mentions rose from 9 to 21. Gist: 'product was sold out when I tried to buy'. BER-HOM-E10 (capacity 219, €74) launched on 2026-10-19 and sold out on 2026-10-23, although it is meant to run until 2026-11-29. Berlin Home revenue is €11.1k/day vs €16.2k in the prior period, €13.3k last year and a €15.2k peer median. The gap to last year is about €2.3k/day, roughly €63k per 28 days.

findings.title: Complaints about seeing too many ads in New York Home (owner: Paid media)
findings.evidence: ad_fatigue: 9 of 57 comments (15.8%) vs 2.0% elsewhere and 3.7% before. Gist: 'sees the brand's ads ten times a day'. Home MER (revenue ÷ marketing spend) is 9.54 vs 10.85 in the prior period and 11.51 last year, still above the 8.66 peer median. I did not check frequency in ad_daily, and the sample is small.

findings.title: Mexico City customers don't know the brand, and the launch is far behind (owner: Brand/Marketing)
findings.evidence: trust_brand: 39 of 230 comments (17.0%) vs 3.1% elsewhere. This is not new: it was 12.7% before. Gist: 'never heard of the brand, is it trustworthy?'. Eight weeks after launch, revenue is €2,231/day, 5% of what Miami (€35.9k) and São Paulo (€49.9k) made at the same age. NPS improved from -22 to -14.

proposed_actions.action: Engineering/Payments: treat as an incident. Find what changed around 2026-10-14 on the iOS payment step in London and Barcelona (app or web release, payment provider, card checks), then roll back or hotfix. Track iOS checkout-to-order daily until it is back at about 62%.
proposed_actions.why: About €975k per 28 days at risk across the two markets, and the London NPS drop of 20 points comes from this.

proposed_actions.action: Ops/Logistics: escalate with the Lisbon carrier or warehouse, proactively tell open orders about the delay, and pause delivery-promise messages in Lisbon until on-time delivery recovers.
proposed_actions.why: Late deliveries make up 30% of Lisbon comments, up from 6%. Lisbon NPS (-39) is the lowest of all markets.

proposed_actions.action: Web/SEO: crawl the New York site for 404s from Google landing URLs, add 301 redirects and resubmit the sitemap.
proposed_actions.why: Customers report broken Google links, and organic-search revenue is down €176k vs the prior 28 days.

proposed_actions.action: Merchandising: restock or extend capacity for BER-HOM-E10, or point traffic to an alternative product. Paid media: cut Berlin Home spend aimed at sold-out items.
proposed_actions.why: The product sold out 4 days after launch with 5 weeks left, and Home revenue is €2.3k/day below last year.

proposed_actions.action: Paid media: add frequency caps and rotate creative for New York Home retargeting.
proposed_actions.why: Complaints about too many ads rose from 3.7% to 15.8% of comments, and MER is down from last year.

proposed_actions.action: Brand/Marketing: add trust signals in Mexico City (reviews, local payment options, returns guarantee).
proposed_actions.why: Lack of trust is the main barrier for a launch running at 5% of earlier launches.

not_problems: Madrid Fashion drops 'wants more range' (22.4%): this is a long-running request (16% before), not new and not a defect. Pass it to the product roadmap, not to incident triage.
Barcelona late deliveries fell from 22 to 7 mentions and website_ux from 13 to 6, so they are improving.

Product quality complaints show no defect cluster: counts are flat in London (13 vs 13) and Berlin (17 vs 21), down in Lisbon (13 vs 23), and up only slightly in Barcelona (21 vs 15) and New York (20 vs 15). None was flagged as significant.
New York NPS improved (-20 to -12), as did Milan (-14 to -3) and Miami (-18 to -13), despite the New York site complaints.
Lisbon revenue is below peers partly because the market is smaller (€37.4k/day last year vs a €44.4k peer median), so only the gap to last year is counted against the delivery problem.
NPS dips in Paris (+2 to -12) and São Paulo (+2 to -14) come from about 80–90 answers each, and no theme is over-represented there. Treat them as possible noise and watch them, rather than acting.

input.summary: If we move money between channels inside each market-line and keep total spend the same, the model expects about €143k more revenue a week (roughly €620k a month). About 58% of that (€83k a week) comes from market-lines where the model fits well. The moves are the same everywhere: take money from Google brand search and Meta retargeting, which add little revenue beyond what the platforms report, and put it into TikTok, YouTube, creators and affiliates. Separately, October overspend came to €123k across Milan, New York, Barcelona and London, mostly on channels that return little for each extra euro.

findings.title: Moving money between channels at the same total budget: +€143k revenue a week (lower bound)
findings.evidence: The plan tool cut off after the top 19 of 44 market-lines, so the 25 smallest gains (each under €5,715 a week) are missing. The 19 visible gains add up to €143,277 a week, about €620k a month at 4.33 weeks per month. By how well the model fits (r2, 0–1): good fit, r2 ≥ 0.7, 12 lines = €83,233 a week, mainly New York Gifts €9,330 (r2 0.899), Paris Home €9,804 (0.718), São Paulo Home €7,520, Fashion drops €7,019, Beauty €6,961 and Gifts €5,715 (r2 0.985–0.993), Paris Gifts €6,829 (0.937), Madrid Home €6,317 (0.801), Miami Home €6,159 (0.991), Milan Home €5,994 (0.748), Madrid Gifts €5,802 (0.936) and Miami Fashion drops €5,783 (0.992). Middling fit, 0.5–0.7: New York Home €12,042, Madrid Fashion drops €6,874 and Paris Fashion drops €6,547 = €25,463. Poor fit, under 0.5: New York Fashion drops €12,560 (0.39), London Home €8,383 (0.467), London Fashion drops €7,597 (0.302) and New York Beauty €6,041 (0.358) = €34,581. Expected revenue rises 3.5–6.1% per line. Gross profit can't be sized because there is no margin data in the hub.

findings.title: Which market-lines the model fits well and which it doesn't
findings.evidence: Gifts fits well everywhere (r2 0.78–0.94), and so do Berlin (0.75–0.94) and Madrid Home (0.80). Beauty fits poorly almost everywhere: London 0.209, Barcelona 0.34, Milan 0.344, New York 0.358, Lisbon 0.373, Madrid 0.502, Amsterdam 0.526. Berlin Beauty (0.83) is the exception. London and New York Fashion drops fit poorly too (0.302 and 0.39). Three reasons to treat even the good fits with care. First, search-interest elasticity is about 0.96 in every model while paid channels are only 0.00–0.08, so a high r2 mostly reflects search demand, not media. Second, the pooled elasticities don't agree with the per-line ones: Meta prospecting is 0.9619 pooled vs about 0.06 per line, which points to collinearity with search. Third, Miami's r2 of 0.99 comes from only 32 weeks of data, a likely sign of overfitting, and São Paulo's 0.99 should be read the same way. The plan also raises small channels by 55–70%, beyond the spend levels the model has seen, so real gains could easily be half of what it estimates. Mexico City has no model.

findings.title: Google brand search is saturated: last-click credits it with 8.95 ROAS, but the model says it adds about 0–1.4
findings.evidence: Over the last 28 days Google brand spent €425,739. First-party last-click ROAS (revenue per € spent) was 8.95, and Google claims 9.85. The model's revenue from the next euro (marginal ROAS) is near zero almost everywhere: 0.00 in Paris Home, Barcelona Fashion drops, Lisbon Gifts and New York Gifts, and 0.05–0.40 in most other lines. The highest are São Paulo Gifts 1.4, São Paulo Home 1.07 and Miami Home 0.93. Last-click is crediting it with demand that would arrive anyway. The plan cuts it by 43–49% in every line.

findings.title: Meta retargeting: Meta claims 2.2 times the revenue our own data shows, and the model says it adds even less
findings.evidence: Last 28 days: spend €348,897. Meta claims €1,188,424 (ROAS 3.41), our first-party data shows €539,086 (ROAS 1.55), and the model's marginal ROAS is 0.11 in Barcelona Beauty, 0.2 in Lisbon Beauty, 0.33 in Barcelona Gifts, 0.63–0.87 in many lines, and only up to 1.65 in Madrid Fashion drops. TikTok also over-claims (platform ROAS 5.83 vs 3.32 first-party). YouTube's platform ROAS of 5.7 is far above its first-party 2.91, but the model agrees YouTube is strong (marginal ROAS 2.8–9.07), so last-click under-credits it.

findings.title: Underfunded channels: YouTube, creators and TikTok are best in every line
findings.evidence: Each of these channels gets only about €600–2,000 a week per line, yet YouTube is the top channel in most lines (São Paulo Home 9.07, Madrid Fashion drops 7.32, Paris Home 6.96, London Home 6.9). Creators are top in São Paulo Gifts and Miami Home (6.28) and TikTok in New York Gifts (5.78). For comparison, Meta prospecting earns 0.75–2.73 and Google generic 0.9–3.11.

findings.title: Moving budget between lines: Beauty earns the least per extra euro and could fund Home and Fashion drops
findings.evidence: Blended marginal ROAS (revenue from the next euro across all channels) is lowest in Lisbon Beauty 0.97, Barcelona Beauty 1.01, Amsterdam Beauty 1.07, Berlin Beauty 1.18, Milan Beauty 1.21 and London Beauty 1.25. It is highest in São Paulo Home 3.62, São Paulo Gifts 3.12, São Paulo Fashion drops 2.85, Madrid Fashion drops 2.74, Miami Home 2.61, Paris Home 2.60 and New York Home 2.60. Example: take 20% of weekly spend from Berlin, Amsterdam, Lisbon and Barcelona Beauty (€2,802 + €2,797 + €2,266 + €3,044 = €10,909 a week, about €47k a month). Those euros earn about 1.06 now and would earn about 2.4–2.6 in Paris Home or Madrid Home, worth up to about €15.7k a week (about €68k a month). That is a ceiling, because returns fall as spend rises. Only Berlin Beauty's numbers come from a good fit (r2 0.83); the other three Beauty donors fit poorly (0.34–0.53).

findings.title: October overspend: €123k over budget in four markets, mostly on low-return channels
findings.evidence: Spend vs budget in October 2026: Milan €301,886 of €252k (119.8%, +€49,886), New York €435,621 of €400k (108.9%, +€35,621), Barcelona €274,626 of €256k (107.3%, +€18,626), London €378,450 of €360k (105.1%, +€18,450). In Aug–Sep all four were within 98–104%. Most of New York's overspend was Google generic in Gifts, Fashion drops and Home: up from €50.8k in September to €78.1k in October, where the model's marginal ROAS is 0.95–1.45. In Milan, Fashion drops Meta prospecting rose €19.7k → €25.4k (marginal ROAS 1.23) and Home Meta retargeting €7.4k → €10.5k (0.64). For November, after 1 day, New York projects to 112.1% and Madrid to 106.1%.

findings.title: Barcelona's organic revenue is down 21.7% on last year while paid spend rose 4.4%
findings.evidence: Last 28 days: organic revenue -24.8% vs the period before and -21.7% vs last year, paid revenue -23.8%, spend +4.4%, MER (revenue per € of marketing) 5.13. London (-18.8% vs last year) and New York (-19.8%) are also down on last year. Because revenue moves almost one-for-one with search interest (elasticity about 0.96), this looks like a fall in demand, not a media problem. Extra spend won't fix it: Barcelona's lines earn only 1.01–1.46 per extra euro.

proposed_actions.action: Make the channel moves now in the 12 well-fitting lines (r2 ≥ 0.7): cut Google brand and Meta retargeting by about 40–49% and raise YouTube, creators, TikTok and affiliates by 50–70%, keeping each line's total the same. Start with Paris Home (Google brand €2,683 → €1,385 and retargeting €2,456 → €1,267 a week; YouTube €1,053 → €1,630 and creators €904 → €1,400) and New York Gifts (Google brand €3,317 → €1,841; TikTok €1,569 → €2,612).
proposed_actions.why: The model expects +€83k a week (about €360k a month), but the real gain could be half that. The 55–70% increases go beyond spend levels the model has seen, and São Paulo and Miami fits are probably overfit.

proposed_actions.action: In the poorly fitting lines (New York and London Fashion drops, London Home, New York Beauty), test the same moves first. Run geo-holdouts that pause Google brand in one region and cut retargeting by 50% for 4 weeks, then roll out.
proposed_actions.why: The model's estimate there is €34.6k a week, but with r2 0.30–0.47 it is not reliable enough to act on directly.

proposed_actions.action: Shift about €10.9k a week (about €47k a month) from Berlin, Amsterdam, Lisbon and Barcelona Beauty to Paris Home and Madrid Home, taking the money mainly from Meta prospecting and retargeting in those Beauty lines.
proposed_actions.why: Those euros earn about 1.06 per € in Beauty vs about 2.4–2.6 in Paris and Madrid Home. That is worth up to about €68k a month, less as returns fall with more spend.

proposed_actions.action: Bring Milan and New York back to budget for November. Cap New York's Google generic at its September level (about €51k a month across Gifts, Fashion drops and Home) and roll back Milan's October increases in Fashion drops Meta prospecting and Home retargeting.
proposed_actions.why: October overspend was €49.9k in Milan and €35.6k in New York, mostly on channels earning 0.64–1.45 per extra euro. New York is already projecting to 112.1% for November.

proposed_actions.action: Judge Meta, TikTok and YouTube on first-party revenue or the model, not on what the platforms report. Treat Google brand's last-click ROAS as an upper limit.
proposed_actions.why: Meta retargeting reports 3.41 ROAS vs 1.55 first-party and about 0.1–1.65 in the model. Google brand shows 8.95 last-click vs about 0–1.4 in the model.

not_problems: Mexico City spending far below budget is a launch ramp, not a delivery failure. It went from 5.7% of budget in September to 21.7% in October (€56.5k of €260k) to a 27.3% projection for November, and spend is up 167%. There is no model for it yet, so its spare budget can't be scored.
November pacing is based on 1 day (3.3% of the month), so Lisbon at 87.9% and London at 90.9% are noise. Aug–Sep, every market except Mexico City was within 93.5–103.9% of budget.
Berlin's organic revenue is down 24.6% on the period before but only 7.3% on last year, so most of the drop is seasonal.
Organic revenue in Paris, Madrid, Lisbon, Milan, Amsterdam, Miami and São Paulo is within about ±5% of the period before and of last year: normal noise.

YouTube's platform ROAS (5.7) is far above its first-party figure (2.91), but the model independently rates it the strongest channel, so last-click under-credits it. That gap is not a reason to cut it.

output.summary: If we move money between channels inside each market-line and keep total spend the same, the model expects about €143k more revenue a week (roughly €620k a month). About 58% of that (€83k a week) comes from market-lines where the model fits well. The moves are the same everywhere: take money from Google brand search and Meta retargeting, which add little revenue beyond what the platforms report, and put it into TikTok, YouTube, creators and affiliates. Separately, October overspend came to €123k across Milan, New York, Barcelona and London, mostly on channels that return little for each extra euro.

findings.title: Moving money between channels at the same total budget: +€143k revenue a week (lower bound)
findings.evidence: The plan tool cut off after the top 19 of 44 market-lines, so the 25 smallest gains (each under €5,715 a week) are missing. The 19 visible gains add up to €143,277 a week, about €620k a month at 4.33 weeks per month. By how well the model fits (r2, 0–1): good fit, r2 ≥ 0.7, 12 lines = €83,233 a week, mainly New York Gifts €9,330 (r2 0.899), Paris Home €9,804 (0.718), São Paulo Home €7,520, Fashion drops €7,019, Beauty €6,961 and Gifts €5,715 (r2 0.985–0.993), Paris Gifts €6,829 (0.937), Madrid Home €6,317 (0.801), Miami Home €6,159 (0.991), Milan Home €5,994 (0.748), Madrid Gifts €5,802 (0.936) and Miami Fashion drops €5,783 (0.992). Middling fit, 0.5–0.7: New York Home €12,042, Madrid Fashion drops €6,874 and Paris Fashion drops €6,547 = €25,463. Poor fit, under 0.5: New York Fashion drops €12,560 (0.39), London Home €8,383 (0.467), London Fashion drops €7,597 (0.302) and New York Beauty €6,041 (0.358) = €34,581. Expected revenue rises 3.5–6.1% per line. Gross profit can't be sized because there is no margin data in the hub.

findings.title: Which market-lines the model fits well and which it doesn't
findings.evidence: Gifts fits well everywhere (r2 0.78–0.94), and so do Berlin (0.75–0.94) and Madrid Home (0.80). Beauty fits poorly almost everywhere: London 0.209, Barcelona 0.34, Milan 0.344, New York 0.358, Lisbon 0.373, Madrid 0.502, Amsterdam 0.526. Berlin Beauty (0.83) is the exception. London and New York Fashion drops fit poorly too (0.302 and 0.39). Three reasons to treat even the good fits with care. First, search-interest elasticity is about 0.96 in every model while paid channels are only 0.00–0.08, so a high r2 mostly reflects search demand, not media. Second, the pooled elasticities don't agree with the per-line ones: Meta prospecting is 0.9619 pooled vs about 0.06 per line, which points to collinearity with search. Third, Miami's r2 of 0.99 comes from only 32 weeks of data, a likely sign of overfitting, and São Paulo's 0.99 should be read the same way. The plan also raises small channels by 55–70%, beyond the spend levels the model has seen, so real gains could easily be half of what it estimates. Mexico City has no model.

findings.title: Google brand search is saturated: last-click credits it with 8.95 ROAS, but the model says it adds about 0–1.4
findings.evidence: Over the last 28 days Google brand spent €425,739. First-party last-click ROAS (revenue per € spent) was 8.95, and Google claims 9.85. The model's revenue from the next euro (marginal ROAS) is near zero almost everywhere: 0.00 in Paris Home, Barcelona Fashion drops, Lisbon Gifts and New York Gifts, and 0.05–0.40 in most other lines. The highest are São Paulo Gifts 1.4, São Paulo Home 1.07 and Miami Home 0.93. Last-click is crediting it with demand that would arrive anyway. The plan cuts it by 43–49% in every line.

findings.title: Meta retargeting: Meta claims 2.2 times the revenue our own data shows, and the model says it adds even less
findings.evidence: Last 28 days: spend €348,897. Meta claims €1,188,424 (ROAS 3.41), our first-party data shows €539,086 (ROAS 1.55), and the model's marginal ROAS is 0.11 in Barcelona Beauty, 0.2 in Lisbon Beauty, 0.33 in Barcelona Gifts, 0.63–0.87 in many lines, and only up to 1.65 in Madrid Fashion drops. TikTok also over-claims (platform ROAS 5.83 vs 3.32 first-party). YouTube's platform ROAS of 5.7 is far above its first-party 2.91, but the model agrees YouTube is strong (marginal ROAS 2.8–9.07), so last-click under-credits it.

findings.title: Underfunded channels: YouTube, creators and TikTok are best in every line
findings.evidence: Each of these channels gets only about €600–2,000 a week per line, yet YouTube is the top channel in most lines (São Paulo Home 9.07, Madrid Fashion drops 7.32, Paris Home 6.96, London Home 6.9). Creators are top in São Paulo Gifts and Miami Home (6.28) and TikTok in New York Gifts (5.78). For comparison, Meta prospecting earns 0.75–2.73 and Google generic 0.9–3.11.

findings.title: Moving budget between lines: Beauty earns the least per extra euro and could fund Home and Fashion drops
findings.evidence: Blended marginal ROAS (revenue from the next euro across all channels) is lowest in Lisbon Beauty 0.97, Barcelona Beauty 1.01, Amsterdam Beauty 1.07, Berlin Beauty 1.18, Milan Beauty 1.21 and London Beauty 1.25. It is highest in São Paulo Home 3.62, São Paulo Gifts 3.12, São Paulo Fashion drops 2.85, Madrid Fashion drops 2.74, Miami Home 2.61, Paris Home 2.60 and New York Home 2.60. Example: take 20% of weekly spend from Berlin, Amsterdam, Lisbon and Barcelona Beauty (€2,802 + €2,797 + €2,266 + €3,044 = €10,909 a week, about €47k a month). Those euros earn about 1.06 now and would earn about 2.4–2.6 in Paris Home or Madrid Home, worth up to about €15.7k a week (about €68k a month). That is a ceiling, because returns fall as spend rises. Only Berlin Beauty's numbers come from a good fit (r2 0.83); the other three Beauty donors fit poorly (0.34–0.53).

findings.title: October overspend: €123k over budget in four markets, mostly on low-return channels
findings.evidence: Spend vs budget in October 2026: Milan €301,886 of €252k (119.8%, +€49,886), New York €435,621 of €400k (108.9%, +€35,621), Barcelona €274,626 of €256k (107.3%, +€18,626), London €378,450 of €360k (105.1%, +€18,450). In Aug–Sep all four were within 98–104%. Most of New York's overspend was Google generic in Gifts, Fashion drops and Home: up from €50.8k in September to €78.1k in October, where the model's marginal ROAS is 0.95–1.45. In Milan, Fashion drops Meta prospecting rose €19.7k → €25.4k (marginal ROAS 1.23) and Home Meta retargeting €7.4k → €10.5k (0.64). For November, after 1 day, New York projects to 112.1% and Madrid to 106.1%.

findings.title: Barcelona's organic revenue is down 21.7% on last year while paid spend rose 4.4%
findings.evidence: Last 28 days: organic revenue -24.8% vs the period before and -21.7% vs last year, paid revenue -23.8%, spend +4.4%, MER (revenue per € of marketing) 5.13. London (-18.8% vs last year) and New York (-19.8%) are also down on last year. Because revenue moves almost one-for-one with search interest (elasticity about 0.96), this looks like a fall in demand, not a media problem. Extra spend won't fix it: Barcelona's lines earn only 1.01–1.46 per extra euro.

proposed_actions.action: Make the channel moves now in the 12 well-fitting lines (r2 ≥ 0.7): cut Google brand and Meta retargeting by about 40–49% and raise YouTube, creators, TikTok and affiliates by 50–70%, keeping each line's total the same. Start with Paris Home (Google brand €2,683 → €1,385 and retargeting €2,456 → €1,267 a week; YouTube €1,053 → €1,630 and creators €904 → €1,400) and New York Gifts (Google brand €3,317 → €1,841; TikTok €1,569 → €2,612).
proposed_actions.why: The model expects +€83k a week (about €360k a month), but the real gain could be half that. The 55–70% increases go beyond spend levels the model has seen, and São Paulo and Miami fits are probably overfit.

proposed_actions.action: In the poorly fitting lines (New York and London Fashion drops, London Home, New York Beauty), test the same moves first. Run geo-holdouts that pause Google brand in one region and cut retargeting by 50% for 4 weeks, then roll out.
proposed_actions.why: The model's estimate there is €34.6k a week, but with r2 0.30–0.47 it is not reliable enough to act on directly.

proposed_actions.action: Shift about €10.9k a week (about €47k a month) from Berlin, Amsterdam, Lisbon and Barcelona Beauty to Paris Home and Madrid Home, taking the money mainly from Meta prospecting and retargeting in those Beauty lines.
proposed_actions.why: Those euros earn about 1.06 per € in Beauty vs about 2.4–2.6 in Paris and Madrid Home. That is worth up to about €68k a month, less as returns fall with more spend.

proposed_actions.action: Bring Milan and New York back to budget for November. Cap New York's Google generic at its September level (about €51k a month across Gifts, Fashion drops and Home) and roll back Milan's October increases in Fashion drops Meta prospecting and Home retargeting.
proposed_actions.why: October overspend was €49.9k in Milan and €35.6k in New York, mostly on channels earning 0.64–1.45 per extra euro. New York is already projecting to 112.1% for November.

proposed_actions.action: Judge Meta, TikTok and YouTube on first-party revenue or the model, not on what the platforms report. Treat Google brand's last-click ROAS as an upper limit.
proposed_actions.why: Meta retargeting reports 3.41 ROAS vs 1.55 first-party and about 0.1–1.65 in the model. Google brand shows 8.95 last-click vs about 0–1.4 in the model.

not_problems: Mexico City spending far below budget is a launch ramp, not a delivery failure. It went from 5.7% of budget in September to 21.7% in October (€56.5k of €260k) to a 27.3% projection for November, and spend is up 167%. There is no model for it yet, so its spare budget can't be scored.
November pacing is based on 1 day (3.3% of the month), so Lisbon at 87.9% and London at 90.9% are noise. Aug–Sep, every market except Mexico City was within 93.5–103.9% of budget.
Berlin's organic revenue is down 24.6% on the period before but only 7.3% on last year, so most of the drop is seasonal.
Organic revenue in Paris, Madrid, Lisbon, Milan, Amsterdam, Miami and São Paulo is within about ±5% of the period before and of last year: normal noise.

YouTube's platform ROAS (5.7) is far above its first-party figure (2.91), but the model independently rates it the strongest channel, so last-click under-credits it. That gap is not a reason to cut it.
